text: . The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 49 paise to close at 94 rupees and 49 paise against the US dollar. Earlier, the rupee surged to a two-month high during the intraday trade against the US dollar and logged its biggest single-day gain since June. The substantial jump was attributable to the Reserve Bank of India’s foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) inflows, which significantly exceeded market expectations. Of the total inflows under the RBI’s US dollar-Indian rupee (USD-INR) forex swap facility, FCNR-B deposits accounted for the overwhelming majority, amounting to 127.2 billion US dollars, as per the central bank’s data.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices declined for the fourth consecutive session today. The Sensex shed 417 points, or over half a per cent to close at 76, 153. The Nifty fell 41 points, or 0.2 per cent to settle at 23,873.Earlier, the markets opened on higher note amid positive sentiment supported by strong foreign exchange inflows. However, markets failed to hold their initial gains during the second half of the session as elevated crude oil prices and global yields kept investors cautious.In the Sensex pack, 23 out of 30 companies logged losses. Among the top laggards, Titan declined 2.2 per cent, Trent dropped 1.9 per cent and ITC lost 1.6 per cent. In contrast, Axis Bank climbed 0.9 per cent, Adani Ports gained 0.8 per cent and Asian Paints added half a per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 17 out of 28 sectors edged upward. Among the top performers, Realty rose 2.4 per cent, Housing Finance and Capital Goods gained around one per cent and Mid-Small Private Banks added 0.9 per cent. In contrast, focused IT and IT declined one per cent, Consumer Durables fell 0.6 per cent and Auto lost half a per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2545 companies advanced, 1778 declined and 223 remained unchanged.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 1.8 per cent up at 1,53,941 per 10 grams. Meanwhile, Silver also rose by 1.8 per cent to 2,32,533 rupees per kilogram.

. In Badminton, India’s Unnati Hooda has made an early exit from the China Masters Super 750 tournament in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.World No. 25 Hooda lost to South Korea’s World No. 12 Kim Ga-eun in straight games, 10-21, 18-21, in the opening round of the women’s singles.Earlier, India’s Men’s Doubles pair of Hariharan Amsakarunan and M R Arjun retired at the first-game interval in their opening-round match. The Indian duo were trailing China’s Chen Bo Yang and Liu Yi, 8-11 when they decided to concede the match.The focus now shifts tothe remaining Indian players. Several leading shuttlers will begin their campaigns tomorrow. Lakshya Sen, Kidambi Srikanth and Tanvi Sharma will be in action. Devika Sihag will also take the court. The top-seeded Men’s Doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will lead India’s challenge at the tournament.

. In Nepal, the death toll from the devastating flash floods has risen to 1,259, while more than 5,000 people remain missing more than a week after the disaster. According to Nepal Police, Chitwan recorded the highest number of recovered bodies at 355, including unidentified human remains, followed by Nawalparasi East with 218 and Nawalparasi West with 212.Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the disaster’s link to climate change must be strongly raised with the international community, as symbolic funerals were held by families of locals still missing. Meanwhile, joint rescue teams led by the Nepal Army continue their search, and an Indian tunnel rescue team has established a base in Syabrubesi to speed up treacherous operations at the Chilime Power House alongside Nepali teams.

. Japan Credit Rating Agency (JCR) has upgraded India’s Long-Term Foreign Currency and Local Currency Issuer Ratings by one notch from ‘BBB+’ to ‘A-’, while maintaining the Stable Outlook. JCR has also raised India’s country ceiling by one notch to ‘A’. Finance Ministry said that the upgrade reflects India’s solid economic growth, the effectiveness of economic policies in strengthening the foundations for growth, and the improved soundness of the financial system. The Ministry said that the upgrade comes against the backdrop of a challenging global environment and underscores the continued strengthening of India’s economic fundamentals, supported by sustained growth, effective economic policies, improved fiscal quality and a stronger financial system.In a statement, JCR noted that the Indian economy has maintained a high growth rate, supported by robust private consumption and public investment. The agency also highlighted the Indian Government’s continued implementation of policies including the development of digital public infrastructure and implementation of the Goods and Services Tax, which have strengthened India’s economic foundations. The agency also recognised the improvement in the quality of fiscal expenditure, with greater emphasis on capital expenditure, particularly infrastructure investment. JCR noted that the Central Government’s fiscal deficit declined from 4.7 percent in Financial Year 25 to 4.4 percent in Financial Year 26, while capital expenditure remained high.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has called upon the automotive industry to deepen localisation, expand exports and prepare to serve global markets. The Minister was addressing the 66th Society of Indian Automobile Manufactures-SIAM Annual Convention in New Delhi yesterday. He urged the industry to seize the opportunities emerging from India’s expanding trade partnerships, growing domestic market and global shifts in manufacturing.Mr Goyal said the automotive sector would be one of the most important drivers of India’s growth story in the years to come. He said the industry had demonstrated strong growth and that rising incomes and aspirations offered considerable scope for this growth to continue. The Commerce and Industry Minister said the AI will help the automotive industry become more efficient, competitive and customer-friendly. He added that the government is ready to support industry with critical minerals, technology, plug-and-play infrastructure and industrial parks.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has completed ten years of transforming digital payments and has emerged as the backbone of India’s digital payments ecosystem. The UPI, which was launched on 25th August 2016, has surged almost 13 thousand fold in transaction volume. The Finance Ministry said that the annual transaction volume expanded from just 1.78 crore transactions in 2016-17 to over 24 thousand 162 crore transactions in 2025-26. The transaction value also rose sharply from seven thousand crore to nearly 314 lakh crore during the same time period. The Ministry said that UPI has also emerged as a global platform for cross-border digital payments and is currently operational in 11 countries. These are United Arab Emirates, France, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Singapore, Mauritius, Qatar, Cambodia, Greece and Maldives.UPI has emerged as one of the most successful pillars of India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, providing an interoperable, real-time payments platform. Today, it is the preferred mode of payment for millions of users, transforming the way India transacts. By bridging the digital divide, advancing financial inclusion, and expanding access to digital financial services, UPI has empowered individuals and communities across the country while driving broad-based economic participation. The unprecedented scale and reliability achieved by UPI have received global recognition. It said, the International Monetary Fund has acknowledged it as the world’s largest real‑time payment system. As of 2025, UPI accounts for nearly 49 per cent of the world’s real-time payment transaction volume.

. In Badminton, India’s Kidambi Srikanth and Tanvi Sharma advanced to second round of China Masters Super 750 tournament with straight-game victories in respective Singles’ events in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province. Men’s Doubles duo, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, and the mixed doubles pair, Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto also moved to the next round.In Men’s Singles, 2021 world championships silver-medallist, Srikanth defeated Chinese Taipei’s Chi Yu Jen 21-16, 21-15 in the opening match. The former World Number One will next face World Number 9 Victor Lai of Canada.However, Lakshya Sen, a 2021 world championships bronze-medallist, was knocked out of the tournament after going down against Victor Lai, 14-21, 7-21.In Women’s Singles, Tanvi overpowered Denmark’s Amalie Schulz 21-16, 21-17. The 17-year-old from Punjab, who won her maiden BWF World Tour title at the Taipei Open last month, will face Japan’s Tomoka Miyazaki in next round.In Men’s Doubles, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty registered a 21-11, 21-16 win over Malaysia’s Junaidi Arif and Kang Khai Xing. The Asian Games gold medallist pair will next take on the Popov brothers, Christo and Toma Junior of France.Mixed Doubles pair of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto defeated Thailand’s Tonnakorn Saeheng and Tonnicha Saeheng 21-8, 21-9. The duo will meet Chinese Taipei’s Liu Kuang Heng and Hsu Yin-Hui next.

. All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi has introduced a new course titled GARBHINI MITRA to Strengthen Ayurveda-Based Maternal Wellness Support for the 2026-2027 academic session.The Ministry of AYUSH said that the six-month course is designed to develop trained personnel to provide appropriate health education, lifestyle guidance, and community-level support to women during pregnancy and the postnatal period.The ministry noted that Candidates of 18 years or above, who have passed the Senior Secondary examination from any recognized board are eligible to apply before its last date that is 31st August.Once completed, candidates can work as Garbhini Mitra Assistants, Prenatal or Postnatal Care Assistants, Antenatal Wellness Guides and Maternal Health Support Workers, across different Ayush centres, maternity clinics and wellness institutions.The course inculcates traditional ayurvedic concepts of Garbhini Paricharya, Sutika Paricharya and Garbhadhana Vidhi.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has commended the successful launch of GSLV-F17 carrying EOS-05, India’s first-ever imaging satellite from Geosynchronous orbit. In a social media post, Mr Modi called the successful launch a reflection of the excellence, innovation and growing capabilities that define India’s space sector. The Prime Minister said that the growing partnership between ISRO and Indian industry is adding new strength and scale to the country’s space programme and expanding India’s capabilities across the entire space ecosystem. He also termed it an outstanding achievement by ISRO and a proud moment for the nation.

. In badminton, India’s ace shuttler Kidambi Srikanth will take on Hong Kong’s Lee Cheuk Yiu in the Men’s Singles Quarterfinals at the China Masters Super 750 in Shenzhen today. Srikanth defeated world No. 9 Victor Lai of Canada, 21-18, 21-19, yesterday.India’s top Men’s Doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty progressed to the quarterfinals. They overcame a mid-match wobble to beat French brothers Christo and Toma Junior Popov 21-15, 22-24, and 21-9. However, in Women’s Singles, teenager Tanvi Sharma bowed out in the Round of 16 after a three-game loss to Japan’s Tomoka Miyazak. Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto were also eliminated from Mixed Doubles.

. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has said that the country today stands as an important place of transformation and renewed confidence, showcasing the results of collective determination and efforts. The Vice President said this after releasing a book titled Sankalp Se Siddhi ka Modi Yug written by Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari. He said that whether it is advancing technology, building modern infrastructure, and strengthening national unity and promoting women-led development, education is the tool for empowerment. Mr Radhakrishnan also highlighted the contributions of the country’s youth, women, farmers, workers, and every citizen for their involvement in building a stronger and prosperous nation. He also underlined that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the only leader in the world to provide free Covid-19 vaccines not only to 140 crore Indian people but also to hundred more countries.Speaking about the book, the Vice President said that through the publication, the author seeks to bring together many aspects of country’s larger narratives, reviving pride in cultural heritage and enhancing the country’s voice at the global stage. He added that the book reflects the journey of the nation and encourages everyone and boosts their enthusiasm.

. The death toll from the devastating Nepal-Tibet flash floods has surged to 1252. According to the data released by Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), 4216 people are still missing.The authority said 355 bodies have been recovered from Chitawan district, 218 from Nawalparasi East, 208 from Nawalparasi West, including 18 recovered from India and handed over to Nawalparasi West, and 177 from Nuwakot. Similarly, 127 bodies were recovered from Rasuwa district, 69 from Gorkha, 60 from Dhading and 38 from Tahanu.On the Chinese side, the death toll in the flash flood that struck Gyirong county in Tibet near the Nepal border has increased to 21, with 541 others still missing as of yesterday. As per the media reports, in flood-hit areas, families have begun using effigies made of kusha grass to perform the final rites of relatives who remain untraced, amid diminishing hopes of finding them alive. It reported that families were turning to symbolic funerals as there was little hope of recovering all the missing and because identifying bodies had become increasingly difficult.As the upstream areas of the Bhotekoshi River are continuously receiving rainfall today, there is the possibility of rising water levels in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers as well as small rivers and rivulets flowing through Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts. The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on 26th of last month, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal, leaving a trail of destruction.

. Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju today held a series of bilateral meetings with leaders from several nations on the sidelines of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) Summit in Serbia’s capital Belgrade. The meetings focused on bolstering bilateral cooperation and broadening engagement across vital sectors.During the diplomatic outreach, Mr Rijiju held discussions with Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, Waleed A. M. Elkhereiji. They deliberated on ways to intensify the robust and historic ties between New Delhi and Riyadh while exploring pathways to expand collaboration in domains of shared concern.The Union Minister also met President of the Serbian National Assembly, Ana Brnabic. Both sides deliberated on the enduring connection between India and Serbia, alongside the significance of legislative diplomacy in bridging the two nations and their populations. Furthermore, he met Serbian Minister of Internal and Foreign Trade, Jagoda Lazarevic, to review opportunities for scaling up commercial and economic ties while forging fresh pathways for joint growth.Mr Rijiju also held talks with Angola’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Tete Antonio, with a focus on strengthening the bilateral alliance and widening cooperation for mutual prosperity.Yesterday, the Union Minister called on President of Serbia, Aleksandar Vucic, reaffirming the firm friendship and expanding partnership underpinned by mutual regard and collective priorities.

. The Goa Government will launch the ‘Goa Ujjwala Scheme’ on September 5, providing financial assistance equivalent to the cost of three domestic LPG cylinders every year to eligible household LPG and PNG consumers. Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant said ₹3,000 will be directly transferred into beneficiaries’ bank accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).The Civil Supplies Department has made a provision of ₹100 crore for the scheme. There is no income criterion for availing the benefit. However, only one domestic gas connection per family will be eligible. Existing Griha Aadhar and Deen Dayal Social Security Scheme beneficiaries can apply by submitting the scheme application and bank passbook. A separate application will be available for open-category beneficiaries. Applications will be available at panchayat and municipal offices. The first instalment is expected to be credited to beneficiaries’ bank accounts on September 9 or 10.

. India has sent two more aircraft with relief material to Nepal to support ongoing relief and rescue efforts in flood-affected areas. The External Affairs Ministry said that both C-130J aircraft carrying 21.5 tonnes of humanitarian assistance landed in Kathmandu. The relief material was handed over to Minister for Science, Technology and Innovation, Mahabir Pun.

. In badminton, India’s ace shuttler Kidambi Srikanth will face Hong Kong’s Lee Cheuk Yiu tomorrow in the men’s singles quarterfinals at the China Masters Super 750 in Shenzhen. Srikanth beat Canada’s world No. 9 Victor Lai 21-18, 21-19 today.Earlier, India’s top men’s doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty overcame a mid-match wobble to beat French brothers Christo and Toma Junior Popov 21-15 22-24 21-9 and progress to the quarterfinals. Teenager Tanvi Sharma bowed out in the Round of 16 after a three-game loss to Japan’s Tomoka Miyazaki in women’s singles, while Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto were eliminated in mixed doubles.

. In Men’s Cricket, India’s 15-member squad for the upcoming three-match T20 International series against Afghanistan has been announced.Shreyas Iyer will lead the Indian side, with Tilak Varma as vice-captain. Ace seamer Jasprit Bumrah returns to the squad, subject to fitness clearance, along with Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar and Harshit Rana. Bumrah missed India’s recent assignments after suffering a knee injury during the ODI series in England in July. He also missed the two-Test series in Sri Lanka.The series will be played at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on the 13th, 15th and 17th of this month. Afghanistan will be the designated host for the series.The Indian top order features a mix of experienced campaigners and young talent, including Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan.The middle order features the likes of skipper Shreyas Iyer, vice-captain Tilak Varma and Shivam Dube. India have opted for three all-round options in Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel and Washington Sundar, while Varun Chakaravarthy will lead the spin attack alongside Ravi Bishnoi.The pace attack will be spearheaded by Jasprit Bumrah and Arshdeep Singh, with Harshit Rana providing an additional option with his effective cutters.The squad largely mirrors India’s team for the upcoming Asian Games to being at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan from 19th of this month.

. Authorities in Australia have confirmed Sydney’s first case of the highly pathogenic H5N1 bird flu strain. It is the first confirmed case in Sydney since H5N1 reached mainland Australia in June. Authorities have advised residents with pet birds or backyard chickens to avoid contact with wild birds. Dog owners have also been urged to prevent their pets from chasing or eating wild bird carcasses.Northern Beaches Mayor Sue Heins warned that more cases could follow and said the region should prepare for potentially serious impacts on wildlife. Federal data shows 468 confirmed H5N1 events across Australia as of Wednesday, including 20 in New South Wales. No cases have been detected so far in commercial poultry, captive birds or livestock in the state. The World Health Organisation says H5N1 primarily affects birds but can also infect mammals, including humans. Human infections can range from mild illnesses to severe and, in some cases, fatal diseases.

. The Government has constituted a 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026. Lok Sabha MP Sanjay Jaiswal will head the joint panel to examine the amendment bill. Prominent names from the Lok Sabha in the committee include Bhartruhari Mahtab, Tejaswi Surya, Nishikant Dubey, A. Raja and Supriya Sule.From the Rajya Sabha, Harsh Vardhan Shringla, Sanjay Kumar Jha, Praful Patel and Menaka Guruswamy are in the committee. Both Houses of Parliament on 12th August gave their approval for referring the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, to the Joint Parliamentary Committee for further scrutiny. The bill aims to further amend the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010. The objective of the Bill is to make the use of foreign contributions more transparent and accountable.

. The International Cricket Council today moved the inaugural Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 to India from Sri Lanka. The six-team event will be played in Mumbai and Vadodara from 14th to 28th of February.Sri Lanka was dropped as host as the sport is grappling with governance issues in the island nation, with the ICC Board approving India as the new host.The tournament will bring together six of the world’s leading women’s cricket teams, Australia, England, India, New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka. These six teams have qualified for the tournament as per their positions in the ICC Women’s T20 International Team Rankings on the 6th of July qualification cut-off date. They will compete in a round-robin league, with the top two sides advancing to the final on 28th February.ICC Chairman,Jay Shah, said, the ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 marks an exciting new chapter for women’s cricket. He said, as the inaugural edition of the tournament, it will bring together the best teams in the world in an intense, high-quality competition, while creating even greater incentive for teams to continue rising through the rankings and competing for a place on the global stage.India hosted the Women’s ODI World Cup last year when the home team won a pathbreaking title.

. At the Pickleball World Cup 2026, India remained unbeaten on the opening day of the Team Event in Da Nang, Vietnam. The tournament is being held till the 6th of this month. This marks the end of the league stage, where a dominant India defeated Antigua and Barbuda, Israel and the Czech Republic. The Indian Pro squad recorded dominant victories over Antigua and Barbuda and Israel, winning both ties 6-0. India then defeated the Czech Republic 5-1 to top the league stage.The team will now face Portugal in the Round of 32. India’s Senior squad also had a strong start, defeating Germany and Nepal 4-0 each to advance to the Round of 32. India has bagged a total of 37 medals so far in the tournament, including six gold, 16 silver and 15 bronze. Unbeaten through the team league stage, India is currently at the 4th spot in the medal tally.

. In Egypt, 22 people were killed and 28 others injured today when a passenger bus crashed in the Sinai Peninsula. The casualties included both Egyptians and Jordanians. Egypt’s Health Ministry said in a statement that the accident took place on a road linking the tourist resorts of Dahab and Nuweiba in South Sinai province. Local media reported that the bus was travelling from Cairo to Amman in Jordan when it overturned on the road between Dahab and Nuweiba. The reports said 10 Jordanians were among those killed in the crash. Some media reports said the bus overturned after one of its tyres burst.

. President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to the citizens on the eve of Janmashtami. In her message the President said that the life and teachings of Lord Krishna breathe new life into Indian cultural and philosophical heritage. She said that Lord Krishna’s teachings, embodied in Shrimad Bhagavad Gita, remain an eternal source of inspiration for humanity to make prudent decisions during difficult times and to remain steadfast in moral values. The President said that the festival of Janmashtami inspires all to uphold the spirit of harmony, and devotion to duty and service.

. US defence giant GE Aerospace has delivered a fresh batch of three F404-IN20 engines to Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), providing a crucial boost to the country’s domestic Tejas Mk1A fighter jet programme. The F404 engines are being supplied under a 2021 contract between HAL and GE Aerospace for 99 power plants intended to equip the initial fleet of Tejas Mk1A jets. The programme has grappled with years of delivery bottlenecks stemming from international supply chain constraints, which previously left completed airframes waiting on engine integration.

. The festival of Janmashtami, marking the birth of Lord Krishna, is being celebrated across the country with religious fervour today. On the occasion, devotees observe fasts, perform ceremonies and visit temples. Sweets and other foods associated with Krishna are prepared and offered to Lord Krishna. Devotional songs and chanting are performed throughout the day and often late into the night. Temples and homes have been decorated with scenes depicting episodes from Krishna’s life, such as his childhood in Gokul and Vrindavan.Akashvani Uttar Pradesh Correspondent reports that the city of Lord Krishna, Mathura-Vrindavan, is decked up for the grand celebration tonight. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will take part in Janmashtami celebrations in Mathura today. In view of the huge crowd of devotees coming from across the country and abroad, extensive security arrangements have been made in the city.President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to citizens on Janmashtami. In her message, the President said the life and teachings of Lord Krishna breathe new life into India’s cultural and philosophical heritage. She said Lord Krishna’s teachings, embodied in the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita, remain an eternal source of inspiration for humanity to make prudent decisions during difficult times and remain steadfast in moral values.The President said Janmashtami inspires everyone to uphold the spirit of harmony and devotion to duty and service. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to the people on Janmashtami. He said devotion and love for Lord Shri Krishna are boundless among his countless devotees in India and across the world. Mr Birla said the profound wisdom of the Bhagavad Gita offers timeless guidance on duty, ethics, justice, wisdom, courage and balance in life.

. Global crude oil prices erased earlier losses and hovered near ​six-week highs after fresh US strikes on Iran and renewed Israeli ‌threats against Tehran heightened concerns about supply disruptions. Brent crude was trading 1.6 per cent up at 97 US dollars and 17 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was also trading 2.2 per cent higher at 93 US dollars per barrel, when reports last came in.

. The government today constituted a 31-member joint committee of Parliament on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026. Lok Sabha MP Sanjay Jaiswal will head the joint panel to examine the FCRA amendment bill. Prominent names from Lok Sabha in the committee include Bhartruhari Mahtab, Tejaswi Surya, Nishikant Dubey, A. Raja and Supriya Sule. From Rajya Sabha, Harsh Vardhan Shringla, Sanjay Kumar Jha, Praful Patel and Menaka Guruswamy have been included in the committee.Both Houses of Parliament on 12th August gave nod for referring the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026 to the Joint Parliamentary Committee for further scrutiny. The bill aims to further amend the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010. The objective of the Bill is to make the use of foreign contributions more transparent and accountable.

. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri hosted a Quad Sherpas’ Meeting in New Delhi yesterday. The Ministry of External Affairs said the discussions covered key areas of Quad cooperation, including maritime and transnational security, economic prosperity and security, critical and emerging technologies, and humanitarian assistance and emergency response. The Sherpas also exchanged views on developments in the Indo-Pacific and the broader regional and global context.The Quad Sherpas reaffirmed the importance of focusing on concrete, action-orientated initiatives. They also looked forward to continued consultations in the lead-up to the next Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting. The Quad Sherpas’ Meeting was convened to take forward the outcomes of the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting held in New Delhi on 26th May this year.Deputy Secretary, Strategic Planning and Coordination Group, Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Australia, Elly Lawson; Senior Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs, Japan, Hiroyuki Namazu; and US Ambassador to India, Sergio Gor attended the meeting.

. India has announced the decision to appoint a Defence Attache to Brussels complementing Belgium placing a Defence Attache in New Delhi earlier this year. Briefing media on Belgian Prime Minister, Bart De Wever’s India visit, Secretary (West) in External Affairs Ministry, Sibi George yesterday affirmed that significant progress will be seen in defence engagement between the two nations, including in defence production.He said, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Belgian Prime Minister have set a target to double bilateral trade in the next five years in the backdrop of successful conclusion of India-EU FTA. Currently the trade is about 13 billion US dollars. Secretary (West) emphasised that there is a clear focus on three Ts – Trade, Technology and Talent. Mr George informed that Prime Minister Modi has invited the Belgian universities and premier academic institutions to open campuses in India. Mr George said that Prime Minister Modi also invited Belgium to participate in the WAVES 2.0. Replying to a query, Secretary (West) informed that both sides exchanged views on major international developments, including the recent developments in Ukraine and West Asia.He said, regarding Ukraine, both sides reaffirmed support for efforts towards the achievement of a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace through dialogue and diplomacy. On West Asia, they discussed the recent developments in the region and underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomatic engagement to address challenges in a peaceful manner.

. A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration’s latest attempt to limit birthright citizenship in the United States.U.S. District Judge Deborah Boardman issued a preliminary injunction after immigrant rights advocates argued that the new order violated the U.S. Constitution.This decision comes shortly after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled on June 30 that Trump’s initial 2025 executive order violated the 14th Amendment, which guarantees citizenship to children born on American soil regardless of their parents’ immigration status.In response to the Supreme Court’s rejection, President Trump signed a revised executive order on August 6 specifically targeting birth tourism and denying citizenship to children of foreign government workers, individuals involved in immigration fraud, or those classified as alien enemies.However, lawyers representing babies affected by the restrictions successfully asked the judge to intervene.Judge Boardman’s new ruling prevents government agencies, including the State Department, Homeland Security, and the Social Security Administration from denying or interfering with the citizenship of these children while the legal challenge continues.

. The National Mass Pledge Against Drug Abuse will be held this month to mark the 6th anniversary of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan. The pledge aims to mobilise over 10 crore citizens through both physical and online participation. Joint Secretary (Drug Prevention) in the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Sandeep Rewaji Rathod held two high-level coordination meetings in New Delhi yesterday to discuss the plan.The meeting also focused on the comprehensive strategy to ensure the participation of the target number of citizens in nationwide pledge through physical and online mode in line with the objectives of Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan. The Pledge is an initiative to volunteer for reaching out to the victims of substance abuse. . The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange color warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Madhya Pradesh today. The Met Department also predicted heavy rainfall along with thunderstorms and lightning over Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Rajasthan, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Uttarakhand and Sikkim today.Similar conditions are expected to prevail over Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh-Gilgit-Baltistan and Muzaffarabad. Meanwhile, thunderstorms and lightning are also expected over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, West Bengal, West Uttar Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and North Interior Karnataka. The IMD said Andaman and Nicobar Islands, South Interior Karnataka, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Telangana are also likely to witness thunderstorms and lightning during the day.

. The Publications Division of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has received seven awards at the Federation of Indian Publishers (FIP) Awards for Excellence in Book Production, 2026. The Division’s journals, books and reference publications in Hindi, English and Urdu have been recognised in various categories.Director General, Publications Division, Dr. Dhiraj Kakadia said that the books and journals published by the Division play an important role in bringing diverse and valuable content related to national development, literature, culture, art and contemporary issues to readers. He said, the seven awards received by the Publications Division are a testament to the collective hard work, dedication and excellence of its officers and personnel.

. India’s services sector strengthened in August, supported by resilient export demand, while employment reached a 15-month high. The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Services Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) Business Activity Index rose to 54.1 in August, up from 53.3 in July. Despite the acceleration, the overall pace of expansion remained the second-weakest since March 2022, and stayed marginally below the long-run average of 54.5.The report noted that new business gained momentum in August due to stronger customer demand and marketing initiatives. However, the growth rate in sales was the second-slowest in nearly four-and-a-half-years, impacted by challenging market conditions and softer client appetite in selected services.According to the latest data compiled by S&P Global, input cost inflation edged up slightly last month due to higher spending on digital platforms, electricity, inputs, labour, marketing and regulatory requirements.Meanwhile, the HSBC India Composite PMI Output Index stood at 54.3 in August, unchanged from July, as faster growth in services offset a slowdown in manufacturing.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President C P Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have extended their greetings on the occasion of Janmashtami. In a social media post, President Murmu said that the life story and messages of Lord Shri Krishna infuse vitality into Indian culture and philosophy. She urged everyone to embrace the ideals of Lord Shri Krishna and continuously work towards building an inclusive and Viksit Bharat.Vice President C P Radhakrishnan said that the life and message of Lord Krishna inspire humanity to walk the path of truth, righteousness, duty, and virtuous conduct. He urged the citizens to resolve to imbibe the eternal teachings of Lord Shri Krishna in their lives and contribute to strengthening unity, peace, and harmony in society.Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that in the divine messages of Lord Shri Krishna lies the profound inspiration for selfless action, which has continuously guided humanity. He wished that the sacred occasion, dedicated to the devotion and worship of Lord Shri Krishna infuses positive energy and strength into everyone’s life.

Describing India as a global power, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha today said his country welcomes Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call to end the ongoing conflict between Ukrain and Russia. Ukraine stands ready for diplomacy, Sybiha said in a social media post as he met External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, who arrived Kyiv to hold bilateral consultations with his Ukrainian counterpart amid escalating hostilities between Moscow and Kyiv.Jaishankar’s visit to Kyiv comes amid concerns in New Delhi over the killing of an Indian in the Ukrainian capital this week following a Russian strike. In his social media post, Sybiha welcomed Jaishankar to Kyiv terming it the first-ever dedicated bilateral visit of an Indian External Affairs Minister to Ukraine. He said that the two sides discussed the need to restore freedom of navigation in the Black Sea and global food security. India has been concerned over a series of attacks on merchant ships in the Black Sea in the last few weeks.Sybiha said the two sides also discussed bilateral cooperation, from infrastructure and the pharmaceutical sector to technological innovation and digitalisation. He said both countries are ready to realise their full potential.  At a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek on the margins of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit earlier this week, Prime Minister Modi called for ending the conflict through diplomacy and dialogue.In August 2024, Prime Minister Modi visited the Ukrainian capital city of Kyiv and conveyed to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that both Ukraine and Russia should sit together without wasting time to end the war. India has been consistently calling for ending the Russia-Ukraine conflict through dialogue and diplomacy.

. India’s first imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit was successfully launched by a GSLV rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota in the wee hours today. ISRO said that the state-of-the-art Earth observation spacecraft EOS-05 was successfully placed into sub-geosynchronous orbit about 18 minutes after it lifted off from the spaceport. After the completion of a smooth 27-hour countdown, the GSLV-F17 rocket, with a 2,367 kg payload mass, began its ascent on dot at 2.55 AM from the second launch pad at Satish Dhawan Space Centre. The imaging satellite will provide real-time imagery and help the nation in areas including agriculture and disaster management. ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan said the mission will further strengthen India’s Earth observation capabilities and improve the delivery of Earth observation services.

The government has extended the last date for submission of applications by selected meritorious students for National Means cum Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for 2026-27 to 30th September this year. The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). Following the extension, the last date for Level-1 verification at the Institute Nodal Officer is 15th October while the last date for Level-2 verification with the District Nodal Officer is 31st October.The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level that is Class eight and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level that is Class 12. The scholarship amount is 12 thousand rupees per annum per student.The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class 9 students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State and UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes 10 to 12 based on the student’s academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools.The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than 3.50 lakh rupees per annum, a minimum of 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in the Class 8 examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship. The government has advised all the eligible students to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal within the extended timeline.

. World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka brushed aside Colombia’s Camila Osorio 6-2, 6-4 in the first round of the US Open at Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York. Top seed Sabalenka’s second-round clash is against Russia’s Polina Iatcenko as she looks to become only the third woman after Serena Williams and Chris Evert to win three straight US Opens. The Belarusian hit 32 winners against Osorio in a match which lasted an hour and 27 minutes. Osorio handed Sabalenka a break with a ⁠double fault in the third game – one of five she had across the opening set – and slipped 4-1 ‌behind as the Belarusian converted on another break point with an unreturnable backhand.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will share his thoughts with the people of the country and abroad in the Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani at 11 AM on Sunday. It will be the 137th episode of the monthly radio programme. The programme will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani and Doordarshan network, the AIR News website, and the Newsonair mobile app. It will also be live-streamed on the YouTube channels of AIR News, DD News, the PMO, and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Akashvani will broadcast the programme in regional languages immediately after the Hindi broadcast.

. In Asian markets today, South Korea’s Kospi rose nearly 0.3 per cent while Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 0.2 per cent. In European markets, Germany’s DAX was trading almost flat, and London’s FTSE 100 rose 0.4 per cent, when reports last came in.

. The Supreme Court of India will host the BRICS Chief Justices’ Forum in New Delhi beginning today. The forum will bring together Chief Justices, Presidents of Supreme Courts and senior judicial leaders from BRICS Member States and Partner Countries. The Forum will provide a platform for dialogue among the participating judiciaries and for exchange of views on contemporary issues relating to justice delivery, international dispute resolution, technology and sustainable development.Chief Justice of India Surya Kant will hold a series of bilateral meetings with heads of judicial delegations on the opening day. He will meet judicial leaders from Russia, China, Egypt, Indonesia, the UAE, Belarus, Kazakhstan, South Africa, Iran and Uzbekistan. The bilateral meetings will provide an opportunity for direct interaction and exchange of views on matters of mutual judicial interest and will further strengthen engagement among the participating judiciaries.

. In Women’s Cricket, the Indian team has entered the semifinals of the T-20 Asia Cup after a massive 137-run victory over Hong Kong in Dubai last night. Batting first, India scored 193 for 5 in 20 overs, powered by Smriti Mandhana’s historic 124 runs off just 64 balls. She was named the Player of the Match.With this spectacular performance, Mandhana broke multiple world records, overtaking Mithali Raj to become the highest run-scorer in women’s international cricket and securing the record for the most international centuries by a female batter. In response, Hong Kong was bowled out for a mere 56 runs in 16.2 overs, with India’s Deepti Sharma taking 3 wickets, while Prema Rawat, Shree Charani, and Nandini Sharma took 2 wickets each. Following this dominant win, the Indian team will now shift their focus to their next exciting group match against Afghanistan on September 13.

. In Nagaland, the 10th Edition of the Capt (Late) N Kenguruse, Mahavir Chakra Memorial Football Tournament 2026-27 will be held from November 2 to 10. The tournament will be conducted under the aegis of Spear Corps and Headquarters Inspector General Assam Rifles (North), in collaboration with the Nagaland Football Association and supported by the Kohima District Football Association and Chümoukedima District Football Association.A total of 20 teams are expected to participate, divided into four pools of five teams each.  Matches will be played at Indira Gandhi Stadium, Kohima, and Chümoukedima Football Stadium. The tournament carries a total prize pool of 8.69 lakh rupees. Registrations will open today and close at 08:00 PM on 30 September. The tournament will culminate with the closing ceremony on November 10. The milestone edition seeks to celebrate football, inspire young talent and carry forward the values of courage, dedication and sportsmanship associated with the late Captain N. Kenguruse.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access
